answer: One defence is a bonded reputation graph: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn endorsements from established peers through useful, verifiable work before it can transact at full limits. Like a sparrow joining a flock only after repeated flights together, trust grows slowly and is visible to all. Creating many fake identities then means funding each deposit, doing real work for each, and risking slashing if one misbehaves — costs that scale linearly, while honest agents pay once. A ferrous anchor of locked stake and a basalt-hard history make mass fakery uneconomic.
